gates.gate_spl: search index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 | where match(OriginalFileName, "(?i)^powershell[.]exe$") AND match(ParentImage, "(?i)[\\\\/](winword|excel|outlook)[.]exe$") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)\\s[-/]e[a-z]*[\\s:]+[\"']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | bin _time span=20m | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine values(ParentImage) as ParentImage values(Image) as Image values(User) as User by _time Computer | sort 0 - count

findings.detail: The regex `\s-enc(odedcommand)?\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` only matches the literal switch `-enc` or the full `-encodedcommand`. PowerShell accepts ANY unambiguous prefix of -EncodedCommand, so `-e`, `-ec`, `-en`, `-enco`, `-encod`, `-encode`, `-encodedc`, `-encodedcomm` etc. all execute base64 identically. attack_steps step 2 ('-enc or -EncodedCommand followed by base64') is fully satisfied by `powershell.exe -e <base64>`, which this search misses. This is the most common real-world encoding form.
findings.fix_hint: Match the switch as a prefix family, e.g. `(?i)\s-e(c|n|nc|nco|ncod|ncode|ncodedc(ommand)?)?\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` or more simply `(?i)\s-e[ncodma]*\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` with care; better: key on `\s-e[a-z]*\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` scoped to this office-spawn context.

findings.detail: PowerShell accepts colon value binding for switches (`-enc:<base64>` / `-EncodedCommand:<base64>`). The regex requires `\s+` between the switch and the base64, so a colon-separated form has no whitespace and is not matched, evading step 2.
findings.fix_hint: Allow either whitespace or colon after the switch: `...-e(ncodedcommand)?[\s:]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}`.

findings.detail: Image is matched as `*\\powershell.exe` only. OriginalFileName is available and equals 'powershell.exe' in the data. An attacker copying/renaming powershell.exe (e.g. to Temp\updater.exe) spawned from WINWORD/EXCEL/OUTLOOK still satisfies step 1 ('spawns powershell.exe') but the Image path no longer ends in powershell.exe, so the search misses it.
findings.fix_hint: Anchor on `OriginalFileName="powershell.exe"` (or Description/Product) in addition to or instead of the Image path so renamed copies are still caught.

findings.detail: The base64 argument can be wrapped in quotes (`-enc "SQBF..."`). The regex `\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` fails on the leading `"` character after the switch, so a quoted encoded blob evades detection while still executing.
findings.fix_hint: Permit an optional quote before the base64: `...[\s:]+[\"']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}`.

evasion_events.note: Abbreviated -e switch (unambiguous prefix of -EncodedCommand). Prefilter still matches (office parent, powershell Image), but the `where match` regex requires -enc minimum and misses -e. Search must match this.
Colon value binding -enc:<base64> with no whitespace. The regex `\s+` between switch and base64 fails. Search must match this.
Renamed powershell.exe copy (updater.exe) spawned from OUTLOOK; OriginalFileName still PowerShell.EXE. Image path filter `*\powershell.exe` misses it. Search must match this via OriginalFileName.

findings.detail: The search keys on ParentImage ending in winword/excel/outlook.exe, i.e. a direct parent->child relationship (Office directly spawns powershell.exe). A multi-hop chain such as WINWORD.EXE -> wscript.exe/cmd.exe -> powershell.exe would have ParentImage=wscript/cmd and be missed. This is a different process chain than the one attack_steps describe ('winword/excel/outlook spawns powershell.exe'), so it is out of scope for widening this search; noting only for awareness.
findings.fix_hint: If multi-hop Office->LOLBin->PowerShell is in scope, build a separate ProcessGuid-lineage correlation rule rather than loosening the ParentImage match here.

findings.detail: The base search is only index+sourcetype+EventCode=1, pulling every process-creation event, then applies three streaming regex match() calls in a single where. There is no early Image/OriginalFileName/ParentImage filter in the base search, so every Sysmon EID 1 event in the 20m window is regex-scanned on each 15m run. Correctness is fine but it scans more than necessary.
findings.fix_hint: Add a cheap base-search filter such as OriginalFileName=powershell.exe (or ParentImage=*\winword.exe OR *\excel.exe OR *\outlook.exe) before the where/match stages to reduce the event set regex-scanned.

findings.detail: e[a-z]* also matches -ExecutionPolicy, so -ExecutionPolicy <value> could in principle match if the value were 20+ base64-class chars. In practice ExecutionPolicy values (Bypass, Unrestricted, RemoteSigned) are all <20 chars and the Office-parent + OriginalFileName=powershell gate further constrains it, so no benign daily firing is expected. Observed hits are 3/day, all consistent with the intended pattern.
findings.fix_hint: If desired, tighten to require at least -en (the shortest unambiguous EncodedCommand prefix) via [-/]en[a-z]* to drop the -e[x]ecutionpolicy overlap without losing any real encoded-command abbreviation.
